limitations: This is a practical gap audit against the shipped catalog, not an exhaustive list of every possible exercise or a prescription for every client.
Muscle roles and difficulty are coaching defaults inferred from the named movement. They are not validated muscle-force measurements or individual screening decisions.
Holds and carries can use the existing Seconds/Minutes prescription metrics. Distance, speed, power, calories and device resistance have no dedicated set fields; these need a separate logging design.
No new relative 1RM percentages, exercise-specific load recommendations, medical protocols or normative testing values were added.
Existing entries, custom names, saved IDs, media and coach overrides remain intact. Name aliases support finding existing entries without changing workout history.
The existing demo links open a YouTube search; these are not individually reviewed video demonstrations. No third-party photographs or instructions were copied.
Seven ambiguous legacy entries remain for coach review. Cardio modalities and specialized rehabilitation protocols are deferred pending suitable measurement and protocol support.

reasons.Hand-Assisted Pistol Squat: Hand support offers a regression from the existing unassisted pistol; unlike the box variation, the coach controls assistance rather than a seated depth stop.
reasons.Dumbbell Deficit Reverse Lunge: A stable front-foot platform changes available range compared with the existing floor reverse lunge. It is not a front-foot-elevated static split squat.
reasons.Seated Barbell Good Morning: Bench support and bent knees change the hinge setup; trunk extensor emphasis differs from the existing standing version.
reasons.Single-Leg Cable Romanian Deadlift: A low pulley changes resistance direction from the existing dumbbell and barbell single-leg hinges. This entry is a hinge, not a combined RDL-and-row.
reasons.Standing Split-Stance Single-Arm Landmin: Adds a standing split-stance option alongside the existing half-kneeling press. Requires a barbell secured in a landmine base; it is a strict press, not a leg-driven push press.
reasons.Dumbbell Scaption Raise (Thumbs Up): Scapular-plane elevation is a distinct option from the existing front and lateral raises. The name makes the thumbs-up variation explicit.
reasons.Cable Serratus Punch: Adds cable-resisted scapular protraction to the existing bodyweight scapular push-up and wall slide. It is not a full elbow-bending chest press.
reasons.Chest-Supported Dumbbell Y Raise: Incline-bench chest support and external load provide a distinct option from the existing floor Y-T-W activation series. Requires an incline bench.

reasons.Hamstring Walkout: Heel steps lengthen and shorten the lever while holding a bridge. This adds a floor option without a curl machine, ball or sliding board; it is distinct from the existing sliding curl.
reasons.Bodyweight Triceps Extension (Fixed Bar): Adds bodyweight elbow-extension isolation against a fixed bar. Unlike a push-up/dip it emphasizes elbow extension with relatively fixed upper arms; body angle changes resistance.
reasons.Band-Assisted Push-Up: Assistance reduces the bodyweight demand and permits a full push-up pattern. The existing Banded Push-Up is the resisted catalog option; the two now have explicit, separate search aliases.
reasons.Standing Banded Overhead Press: Fills the missing vertical band press for sessions without dumbbells or a press machine. Existing band chest presses remain horizontal pushing options.
reasons.Supported Kneeling-to-Standing: Adds a hand-supported floor-to-standing transfer, which is a different task from a chair sit-to-stand or a step-up. A stable support and tolerated kneeling position are part of the setup.
reasons.Inchworm: Adds a walking hinge-to-plank warm-up movement. It is distinct from the existing Plank Walk-Up, which transitions between forearms and hands. Hamstring lengthening does not become direct hamstring resistance volume.

deferred.reason: The current corrective selection maps Stretch mode to timed holds and posture-derived overactive muscles. Do not misclassify moving hip/thoracic/ankle drills just to list them.

Use the existing prescription and notes where no distinct exercise selection is needed.

reasons.Landmine Rotation: Adds a standing rotational core task around a fixed barbell pivot, distinct from the existing landmine presses, cable wood chop and medicine-ball throws. This is the controlled rotation, not a rotational press.
reasons.Banded Face Pull: Adds a band option for the combined pull/scapular movement when a cable stack is unavailable. The existing band pull-apart has a different elbow/shoulder action and is not treated as the same exercise.
reasons.Banded Overhead Triceps Extension: Provides an overhead elbow-extension option without a cable stack or dumbbell. It is distinct from the existing band pushdown because the upper arm is overhead.
reasons.Dumbbell Wrist Radial and Ulnar Deviatio: Adds side-to-side wrist movement, distinct from wrist flexion/extension and forearm pronation/supination. Both directions share one canonical exercise and aliases rather than inflating the count with two entries.

reasons.Hip Hike (Step): Adds a controlled, stance-side hip-abductor task with the foot fixed and the pelvis moving. Unlike the existing step-down, the support knee stays relatively straight; unlike open-chain hip abduction, the free leg is not being lifted sideways.
reasons.L-Sit Hold (Parallel Bars): Adds straight-arm supported hip/trunk flexion held isometrically, distinct from a hanging leg raise, lying leg raise or hollow hold. This entry denotes the straight-leg supported hold, not a hanging or tucked variant.
reasons.Seated Pike Leg Lift: Adds dynamic active hip flexion from a seated, already-flexed hip position. It is a floor-based compression option rather than a supine or hanging leg raise; it does not require holding the whole body above the floor like an L-sit.

deferred.candidate: Tuck, one-leg and hanging L-sit variants
deferred.reason: Do not multiply the new family in the same batch; first establish the straight-leg supported hold and its measurement. Do not label a tucked or hanging version as the same recorded standard.
Existing wide rows, rear-delt flies and face pulls cover the immediate use cases; no distinct equipment or selection need was established in this audit.
Potential future additions belong in the existing Stretch pathway. The current live New Exercise form cannot set that mode, so do not create incorrectly mapped strength rows just to add them now.

reasons.Floor Sit-Up: Adds full floor-to-upright trunk/hip flexion rather than the smaller trunk-flexion task in the existing abdominal crunch. This entry is not a GHD sit-up or a separate equipment variation.
reasons.Dumbbell Side Bend: Adds loaded lateral trunk flexion. The existing side plank and suitcase carry resist lateral movement; Russian twists, wood chops and landmine rotations use rotational tasks. Wrist side-bend aliases remain separate and the exact trunk exercise ranks first.
reasons.Single-Arm Kettlebell Clean: Adds a one-kettlebell hinge-to-rack movement. It differs from the existing kettlebell swing finish and the existing barbell clean technique. It is not a clean-and-press combination or a kettlebell snatch.
reasons.Barbell Thruster: Adds one continuous front-squat-to-overhead movement. The full squat and linked drive distinguish it from a push press or separately prescribed squat and press sets. One barbell load applies to the whole repetition.

reasons.Seated Leg Curl: Adds a seated machine knee-flexion option; existing ball/slider curls and Nordic curls use different support and loading.
reasons.Machine Chest Press: Adds a supported machine horizontal press, distinct from the existing barbell, dumbbell and cable presses.
reasons.Assisted Pull-Up: Adds a machine-assisted vertical pull for a scalable pull-up prescription; existing unassisted and scapular pull-ups do not supply machine assistance.
reasons.Rope Triceps Pushdown: Adds a cable elbow-extension option with arms at the sides, distinct from overhead and cross-body extensions.
reasons.Cable Lateral Raise: Adds cable resistance for shoulder abduction; the existing unspecified Demo Lateral Raise is preserved rather than assumed to represent this setup.
reasons.Pallof Press: Adds a cable anti-rotation trunk exercise; it is not a rotating wood chop, lateral side bend or plank.
